the learned ranker in web search

The link-analysis models all compute an eigenvector of a link matrix by power iteration; they differ in where the random walk restarts (everywhere, at a fixed set, or nowhere) and in which graph they walk (the whole web or a query-specific base set). The learning-to-rank families can use the same model and differ in the unit of training: one document, one pair, or one list. A modern search engine uses link analysis to produce features and learning to rank to combine them, and a recommendation feed reuses both: random walks and embeddings to generate candidates, and a learned multi-task ranker to order them.

Web search differs from classical retrieval in an uncurated, adversarial collection, short and ambiguous queries, huge result sets with nearly equal term scores, and a link graph that reveals which pages people consider important. The engine serves the intent most users mean, composes the result page for that intent, and relies on a crawler that collects the evidence about each page that the page itself does not provide.

Content signals go beyond term counts: proximity rewards query terms that appear close together, BM25F weights fields before a single saturation, anchor text describes a page in other people’s words, counted with one vote per domain, and location, language, and site quality adapt the ranking to the user and the source.
PageRank is the stationary distribution of a random surfer and measures global prominence, not relevance; HITS computes topic-specific hubs and authorities on a query-dependent subgraph.

Learning to rank combines hundreds of signals; pairwise and listwise objectives target the order of results, and LambdaRank weights each pair by its effect on nDCG. Clicks are abundant training labels but must be corrected for position bias.

Feeds rank without a query, with the same staged design: embeddings and the social graph supply candidates, a learned ranker predicts the user’s reactions, and the weights on these predictions decide what the platform optimizes.
